title: Normalized derived global sections after pro-etale direct image
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f:T\to Y$ and $g:Y\to W$ be morphisms of $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module categories on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and their direct images and exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Derived global sections mean the right derived evaluation at the final object; use the finite derived direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

There is a canonical natural isomorphism of functors on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$
$$\ell_f:R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*(-))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(T,-).$$
On a bounded-below K-injective representative $J$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] of $L$ it is induced by the identity of section complexes $\Gamma(Y,f_*J)=\Gamma(T,J)$. This is natural for all derived morphisms, not only chain maps between specified complexes, and compatible with shifts. For the canonical direct-image composition comparison $c_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\cong Rg_*Rf_*$ [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], one has
$$\ell_{gf,L}=\ell_{f,L}\circ\ell_{g,Rf_*L}\circ R\Gamma(W,c_{g,f,L}).$$
The comparison for an identity is the identity. If $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], the composite
$$R\Gamma(T,L)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(T,\eta_j)}R\Gamma(T,Rj_*j^*L)\xrightarrow{\ell_{j,j^*L}}R\Gamma(U,j^*L)$$
is the canonical restriction map, where $\eta_j$ is the open adjunction unit. In particular these comparisons identify derived global sections of a pushed-forward support-localization triangle with derived global sections of the original triangle, with the same third arrow and its shift comparison.

proof.text: Use the published ordinary module adjunction transported along the coefficient direct-image identification. Exactness of its left adjoint makes the actual sectionwise direct image preserve K-injectives. For an arbitrary K-injective J, specialize the universal right-derived compositor factorization to J and cancel the invertible derived units. This gives precisely the four-factor evaluation formula; no bounded-below replacement is needed. The coefficient identification uses Mathlib pushforwardCongr on the same adjunct coefficient equality, so its hom and inverse act identically on underlying sections without unfolding equality elimination.

proof.text: The canonical right-derived unit commutes with shifts. The right-derived compositor induced by the terminal evaluation isomorphism therefore commutes with the published shift comparisons. Its component equation is the asserted shift formula.

source.place: Tags 05SU and 070Y; canonical right-derived shift comparison

proof.text: Realize ordinary ring-module sections through the intrinsic scalar equivalence. The sheafification unit on the underlying sheaf is objectwise invertible. Compose this unit with the equivalence counit to obtain a bijective realization of every section, natural in modules and restriction maps. The normalized intrinsic direct-image comparison carries this realization to the same section on the base-changed object. Consequently the published terminal comparison is restriction along the canonical inverse terminal-object map.

source.place: Tag 0D6H; final-object evaluation and intrinsic scalar realization

proof.text: Transport the ordinary module direct-image compositor through the coefficient identification; it still acts on sections by restriction along the fibre-product associator. Naturality of adjunction conjugation identifies it as the mate of the published module inverse-image compositor. The localization compatibility theorem identifies its derived compositor with the inverse of the displayed ordinary derived direct-image comparison. On terminal sections the two composite restriction maps agree because both are arrows to the same terminal object. The universal property of the triple right-derived functor carries this equality to every derived object, giving the composition formula.

source.place: Tag 0D6E; adjunction mate and composition of final-object evaluation

proof.text: For the identity map use the published normalized inverse-image module isomorphism, its tensor-unit formula, its termwise comparison and its localization. The coprojection formula and naturality show that the ordinary unit, terminal evaluation and identity inverse-image comparison compose to the identity on sections. The unit-Leray chain formula on K-injectives, followed by naturality along a K-injective model isomorphism, identifies the derived evaluation with the mate of this same localized inverse-image comparison.

source.place: Tag 0DVC; identity-unit normalization and the unit-Leray chain formula

proof.text: For an open immersion apply the existing unit-Leray chain formula to the specified K-injective complexes and the actual resolution map. The transported ordinary adjunction unit followed by the transported terminal comparison is the published unit-Leray section unit: cancel the coefficient identification and its inverse. Substitution gives the open-unit equation, with no additional resolution or boundedness argument.
